speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger. To begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any redness or warmth in the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Gamekeeper's Thumb (Ulnar Collateral Ligament Injury) of the right ring finger.

*Note: While the injury described (jersey pull) is classic for Gamekeeper's Thumb, this condition typically affects the **thumb**, not the ring finger. Given the specific location (ring finger) and mechanism (hyperextension or forced abduction), the diagnosis is more likely a **Volar Plate Injury** or **Mallet Finger** of the right ring finger. I will proceed with imaging to confirm the extent of ligamentous or bony injury.*

REQUEST IMAGES: Right Hand X-Ray (AP, Lateral, Oblique).
REQUEST TEST: Right Hand MRI (to assess collateral ligament integrity if X-ray is normal).

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
